BK Technologies Reports Third Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026 Results

 

Third Quarter 2026 Results Summary:

 

 

●

Revenue: Revenue increased by 3.6% to $25.3 million.

 

 

●

Gross margins: Gross margin reaches 50.7%, expanding from 49.9%.

 

 

●

Net income: Net income of $3.7 million increased by 9%, outpacing revenue growth.

 

 

●

Free Cash Flow: TTM Free Cash Flow After-tax 1 reaches $18.9 million, a 25% year-over-year increase.

 

 

●

Balance sheet: Cash position grows to $29.2 million as of September 30, 2026, a $6.4 million increase compared to $22.8 million as of December 31, 2025.

 

 

●

Working Capital: $48.8 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $11.4 million compared to December 31, 2025.

 

 

●

Strategic Investment: $3.0 million invested in Tango Tango broadens exposure within mission-critical software solutions

 

 

●

Capital Allocation: Doubled the share repurchase authorization to $10 million, with $8.4 million available, underscoring confidence in the Company’s long-term growth and commitment to shareholder value

 

WEST MELBOURNE, Fla. Nov 12, 2026 / BK Technologies Corporation (NYSE American: BKTI) (the “Company,” “BK Technologies”), a provider of advanced public safety communications solutions, today announced financial and operating results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 ended September 30, 2026. The Company will host a conference call today, November 12, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time.

 

 

1  Represents a non-GAAP financial measure. Refer to the section entitled “Use of Non-GAAP Measures” and Reconciliation to GAAP later in this press release.

 

 

John Suzuki, CEO of BK Technologies, commented, “Our third quarter results underscore the durability of our business model and demonstrate our ability to consistently deliver profitable growth. Federal demand was a key growth driver leading to record third quarter revenue of $25.3 million, a gross margin above 50% and an increase in net income of 9% that outpaced revenue growth. The U.S. Forest Service was our primary federal customer in the quarter, taking delivery of 3,000 of our new BKR 5000 Orange radios. We developed this specialized variant of our radio exclusively for the U.S. Forest Service, and it has now been adopted as their new standard radio. Our leadership in wildland fire was built by listening to customers and solving their real-world operational challenges. We are bringing that same customer-focused approach to the broader market with our multiband BKR Series. We ended the quarter with $29.2 million in cash, no debt and $18.9 million in after-tax free cash flow generated over the trailing twelve months. Our strong financial position enables us to fund our product roadmap and make strategic investments in support of our Vision 2030 objectives.

 

“We also continued to execute on our operational and strategic priorities. Our new El Paso distribution center, operated with East West Manufacturing, came online and commenced customer shipments during the quarter. This facility expands our footprint and brings us closer to more customers, expediting factory-to-customer lead times considerably, and represents another example of our commitment to serving first responders with the products they demand most. We continue to strengthen our competitive positioning through diligent investments, proactively identifying opportunities in an evolving industry. Our $3.0 million convertible note strategic investment in Tango Tango expands our exposure to mission-critical software, creates a two-way commercial channel for BK radios and broadens the interoperability ecosystem around InteropONE. It is another step in our evolution from radio manufacturer to public safety technology company.

 

“Subsequent to quarter end, and as previously disclosed, our West Melbourne headquarters experienced a partial roof collapse during a severe thunderstorm on October 8. Most importantly, the incident occurred after business hours, and no employees were injured. Our team responded immediately, activating our emergency recovery plan within the first hour and working diligently to restore affected operations. We are exceptionally proud of how our employees have responded to this unforeseen challenge.

 

“While the incident temporarily disrupted production of our BKR 9000 radios, our underlying business fundamentals and long-term strategic priorities remain unchanged. We expect the resulting shipment delays to be a matter of timing rather than lost business, with affected shipments anticipated to move into 2027 as production returns to normal levels during the first quarter.

 

 

“Importantly, development of our BKR 9500 in-vehicle multiband radio continues to progress. Field validation on live customer systems has performed well, FCC certification is expected by year-end, and we remain on track to achieve mass production by March 2027. We continue to make meaningful progress on the product initiatives that will drive BK Technologies' next phase of growth.

 

“Reflecting the anticipated deferral of BKR 9000 shipments, we are updating our full-year 2026 outlook to approximately $85 million in revenue, GAAP diluted EPS of $2.40, and non-GAAP adjusted diluted EPS of $3.15, while reaffirming our gross margin target of at least 50%. Our updated earnings guidance excludes potential recoveries under our business interruption insurance coverage and potential refunds of previously paid tariffs.

 

“We believe it is important to distinguish this temporary operational disruption from the underlying trajectory of our business. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $29.2 million in cash and no debt at quarter-end, our gross margins remain above 50%, and our investments in new products and software continue to advance. None of these underlying strengths has changed because of the October 8 event.

 

“I want to thank our employees, customers, business partners, and the City of West Melbourne for their extraordinary efforts and support. We remain confident in our ability to restore normal operations, fulfill our customer commitments, and execute our Vision 2030 strategy.”

 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Review

 

Revenue of $25.3 million increased 3.6% compared to $24.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, driven by strong federal order activity, particularly from the U.S. Forest Service.

 

Gross margin of 50.7% expanded by over 70 basis points compared to 49.9% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to favorable product mix and continued customer adoption of both the BKR 9000 multiband radio and BKR 5000 single band.

 

Selling, General & Administrative expenses totaled $8.4 million, compared with $7.3 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in Selling, General and Administrative expenses for the quarter was primarily driven by planned hardware investments in the BKR9500 in-vehicle multiband radio platform and continued advances with the BK ONE software ecosystem.

 

 

Operating income was $4.4 million compared with $4.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. Operating margin declined to 17.5% from 19.8% in the year ago quarter, impacted primarily by higher engineering expenses.

 

BK Technologies recorded net income of $3.7 million, or $0.99 per basic and $0.93 per diluted share, compared with $3.4 million, or $0.93 per basic and $0.87 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. The net income expansion was driven by strong financial performance and lower income tax rate.

 

The Company reported non-GAAP adjusted earnings1 of $4.7 million, or $1.24 per basic and $1.16 per diluted share, compared to $4.9 million, or $1.32 per basic and $1.24 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.

 

Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA1 for the third quarter of 2026 was $5.2 million, compared with $5.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA1 margin of 20.5% compared to 21.5% in the third quarter of 2025.

 

Working capital totaled $48.8 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with $37.3 million as of December 31, 2025. Cash, cash equivalents and trade receivables totaled $46.5 million, representing approximately 95% of working capital, as of September 30, 2026, compared with $30.0 million, or approximately 80% of total working capital at year-end 2025. The Company ended the quarter with no debt.

 

The Company's Board of Directors doubled its authorized share repurchase program to $10 million, with approximately $8.4 million currently available for repurchases, underscoring its confidence in BK Technologies' long-term growth prospects, strong financial position, and commitment to enhancing shareholder value. The expanded authorization reinforces the Company's disciplined approach to capital allocation while providing flexibility to opportunistically repurchase shares in the open market, subject to market conditions and other considerations. The program does not obligate the Company to repurchase any specific number of shares and may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time.

 

 

1  Represents a non-GAAP financial measure. Refer to the section entitled “Use of Non-GAAP Measures” and Reconciliation to GAAP later in this press release.

 

 

Nine Months 2026 Financial Review

 

Revenue of $70.0 million increased 8.3% compared to $64.6 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

 

Gross margin of 51.4% expanded by 320 basis points as compared to 48.2% in the same period last year.

 

Selling, General & Administrative expenses totaled $24.4 million, compared with $19.4 million for the prior year period.

 

Operating income totaled $11.5 million, relatively unchanged compared with $11.8 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

 

BK Technologies recorded net income of $9.7 million or $2.56 per basic and $2.39 per diluted share, compared with net income of $9.3 million or $2.56 per basic and $2.38 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

 

The Company reported non-GAAP adjusted earnings1 of $12.3 million, or $3.26 per basic and $3.04 per diluted share, compared to $12.4 million, or $3.39 per basic and $3.16 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

 

Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA1 was $13.7 million, compared with $12.9 million in the first nine months of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA1 margin of 19.6% compares to 20.0% in the same period a year ago.

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

BK Technologies prepares its consolidated financial statements in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). In addition to disclosing financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, the Company discloses non-GAAP financial measures. Management believes the non-GAAP financial measures discussed in this release are important to the reader of the Consolidated Financial Statements. The Company has provided the non-GAAP financial information presented in the press release, which is not calculated or presented in accordance with GAAP, as information supplemental and in addition to the financial measures presented in the press release that are calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. Such non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered superior to, as a substitute for or alternative to, and should be considered in conjunction with the GAAP financial measures presented in the press release. The non-GAAP financial measures in the press release may differ from similar measures used by other companies.

 

Adjusted Earnings Before Interest Taxes Depreciation and Amortization (Adjusted EBITDA). Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are considered non-GAAP financial measures under the SEC’s rules because they exclude certain amounts included in net income provided in the statement of operations attributable to the Company calculated in accordance with GAAP, the most directly comparable financial measure calculated in accordance with GAAP. Management believes Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin can help the investors better understand operational factors associated with the Company’s financial performance because it excludes the following from consideration: interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, and infrequent or unusual losses or gains (i.e., non-recurring and incremental restructuring charges that are not expected to be routinely incurred year over year because of the Company’s strategy and operating experience). Adjusted EBITDA margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by total revenue. See Reconciliation to GAAP below for calculation methodology and details regarding Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin.

 

 

Adjusted earnings per share (Adjusted EPS). Adjusted EPS is considered a non-GAAP financial measure under the SEC’s rules because it excludes certain amounts included in the basic and diluted earnings per share attributable to the Company calculated in accordance with GAAP EPS, the most directly comparable financial measure calculated in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted EPS is a non-GAAP financial measure that adjusts GAAP EPS for expense items that are typically strategic in nature or that management otherwise does not view as reflecting the operating performance of the Company. Management believes Adjusted EPS can help the reader better understand the operating performance of the core businesses and their ability to generate earnings. The Company has non-cash charges for stock-based compensation that do not reflect the operating performance of the LMR and Solutions businesses. The Company also recorded a one-time, non-cash income tax provision expense for NOL carryforwards during the second, third and fourth quarters of 2025. Management believes that these one-time charges do not reflect the operational profitability of the business for the second, third and fourth quarters of 2025 compared to prior periods. See Reconciliation to GAAP below for calculation methodology and details regarding Adjusted EPS.

 

Free cash flow after tax (FCFAT). Free Cash flow After-tax is considered a non-GAAP financial measure under the SEC’s rules.  FCFAT is used in addition to and in conjunction with results presented in accordance with GAAP, and FCFAT should not be relied upon to the exclusion of GAAP financial measures. Management strongly encourages investors to review our financial statements and publicly-filed reports in their entirety and to not rely on any single financial measure. FCFAT, which we reconcile to “net income,” adjusted for interest income or expense, depreciation and amortization and income taxes, as further adjusted for non-cash stock-based compensation expense and non-cash deferred income tax provision or expense, is a measure of cash flow from operations.  Management also views FCFAT, as a measure of the Company’s ability to reduce debt, add to cash balances, pay dividends, and repurchase stock. FCFAT has limitations due to the fact that it does not represent the residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures. For example, FCFAT does not incorporate payments made on finance lease obligations or required debt service payments. In addition, different companies define FCFAT differently. Therefore, we believe it is important to view FCFAT as a complement to our entire consolidated statements of consolidated operations and cash flows. FCFAT conversion is useful to investors for the foregoing reasons and as a measure of the rate at which the Company converts its net income reported in accordance with GAAP to cash inflows, which helps investors assess whether the Company is generating sufficient cash flow to provide an adequate return.

 

 

We do not provide reconciliations of forward-looking non-GAAP guidance due to the inherent difficulty in quantifying certain items necessary to provide such reconciliations as a result of their unknown effect, timing and potential significance.

 

About BK Technologies

BK Technologies Corporation (NYSE American: BKTI) manufactures high-specification communications equipment of unsurpassed reliability and value for public safety and government agencies. BK’s BKR 9000 handheld multiband radio and next generation BKR9500 in-vehicle multiband radio combines advanced features with rugged durability and interoperability to meet the critical demands of first responders. BK’s Solutions business unit, which includes the BK ONE family of offerings, combines land mobile radio (LMR) and LTE/5G to create seamless connectivity among first responders for planned and emergency events. BK Technologies is headquartered in West Melbourne, Florida. For more information, visit www.bktechnologies.com.
